newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AMLC Beef Weekly - Australian export prices.
newsitem.headline: AMLC Beef Weekly - Australian export prices.

text.p: Australian Meat and Livestock Corp's (AMLC) weekly export prices are as follows:
AUSTRALIAN EXPORT PRICES TO U.S. IN U.S. CENTS/LB, CIF.
Bull (95 Chemical Lean) 93 -3 on last week
AUSTRALIAN EXPORT PRICES TO JAPAN IN U.S. CENTS/LB CIF.
Chilled grassfed fullsets 126 -2 on last week

AMLC COMMENTARY: Handy falls of rain were received across much of Australia this week, with the heaviest occuring in the areas where it was most needed. Across Victoria and South Australia, falls of 25-50 mm were recorded, while in Tasmania most falls were over 50 mm.

This break will give producers, especially in the southern areas, an opportunity to plant fodder crops and winter cereal crops. However, the wider benefits of the rain will be dependent on growing conditions over the next few weeks, before winter sets in.

Livestock markets should be assisted by this rainfall in the coming weeks as numbers offered through the saleyard system are likely to decline at the same time as restocker demand lifts, particularly on the part of those producers who have used their acreage conservatively over spring-summer period. This should increase compeition in the yard among those endeavouring to source stock.
Although the general saleyard price trend over the past fortnight has been upward, this has contrasted with price movements in markets further downstream.
In the U.S. prices for manufacturing beef moved down again this week, pressured by heavier supplies out of Australia and New Zealand and slow demand at retail and food service level.

Prices for imported beef fell between 1-4 USc/lb (2-9Ac/kg). The heaviest falls, reserved for 90CL cow beef, are linked to heavy cow slaughter in both Australia and New Zealand since the end of March.

In the Japanese market, export offer prices for Australian beef generally fell by 2-5c/lb (4-13Ac/kg). The exceptions were cuberoll and tenderloin, which suffered heavy falls of 10 and 15USc/lb (25-35Ac/kg) respectively.

With the Golden Week over and heavier offers from the U.S. expected in the coming months, the outlook for the Japanese market is one of difficult conditions unless demand recovers to more normal levels.

One factor that may benefit Australian exporters is the strengthening in the yen. The Japanese government has come under intense pressure from its trading partners to intervene inthe exchange rate market. In the past week, the Japanese currency has firmed three yen against the US$.
